newsitem.title: USA: Saudi barley needs 5.8 Mln tonnes 97/98 - US attache.
newsitem.headline: Saudi barley needs 5.8 Mln tonnes 97/98 - US attache.

text.p: Saudi Arabia, the world's leading barley importer, will purchase 5.6 million tonnes of barley in 1996/97 and 5.8 million in 1997/98, the U.S. attache in Riyahd wrote in a report released Wednesday.
The report also forecast wheat imports of 2,000 tonnes and rice imports of 675 tonnes in 1996/97, which ends June 30.
"Based on actual imports to date, the ATO (agricultural trade office) believes Saudi Arabia will import 5.6 million tonnes of barley in 1996/97," the attache wrote.
Imports for 1997/98 were forecast for 5.8 million tonnes. In 1995/96, Saudi Arabia imported 3.5 million tonnes.

The Grain Silos and Flour Mills Organization, the government agency that oversees farm production and grain imports, "issued its most recent barley tender on January 6, 1997 for February/March arrival (1.2 million tonnes)," the attache wrote.

"Analysts expect a tender will be issued soon to cover April/May. A new tender in the order of 1 MMT will result in total imports of 4.2 million metric tons during October 1996 - May 97. During the June-September 1997 period, ATO/Riyadh anticipates additional purchases of 1.4 million MT."
The government quota for barley production was expected to be set at one million tonnes but the harvest likely would be lower, the attache wrote.
Livestock consume most of the barley imports. Poor pasture conditions this year were expected to increase consumption.

"Barley consumption in the next few years is expected to increase significantly as poultry, dairy and sheep breeding & fattening projects continue to expand," the report said. "However, it is important to note that the quanties of barley used is dependent to a signficant degree on the level of subsidies provided by the government to end users. As noted...the government recently increased the official retail price of barley by 37 percent."
